Calcifying Epithelial Odontogenic Tumor: The presence of cyst formation with solid components, whorled masses of spindle cells and sheets, rings of columnar cells with duct-like appearance, and presence of calcification are consistent with CEOT. Additionally, the unicystic radiolucent area and solid tumor with spindle cells further support this diagnosis.
Adenomatoid Odontogenic Tumor (AOT): The cystic radiolucency associated with an ectopic tooth, absence of root resorption, and sheets and plexiform strands of epithelium are consistent with AOT. The presence of cyst formation, plexiform strands, duct-like appearance, and rings of columnar cells also support this diagnosis.
